institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses that were available were different than the ones I could find at home, and offered a new academic direction. Also I really appreciate being able to communicate with everyone, and since I speak Danish and English I found it very nice that I could talk normally with the Norwegians (local). I also found it interesting to experience  a new climate.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very nice to be in Tromsø, and I really liked that is quite small, yet still has a town, where you can do things. And that it has the feel of a University town.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I don't feel like I got a lot of information, and since the university went on vacation already in the end of June (before we had gotten any final information) it was had to ask them about what to do and when to arrive or to get information about when the semester ended. They did however send out several mails about updated corona rules that we needed to know in order to get into the country.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I contacted a girl from my student housing who helped us get into the flat, where we could leave our luggage. And a couple of weeks into my semester we had a nice campus and city tour.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I was not very impressed with the information or help we got, but you were able to find answers to your questions on your own without to much trouble.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I applied for housing the first day it was possible (for autumn semester around 15. marts) and only heard back from the agency 3 weeks before my arrival to Norway (and semester start). Samskipnaden took a long time, and I know quite a few people who could not get a place, but there are also very nice private housings in Tromsø.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in Mortensness, which is a little far from the city. but overall a very nice place. Ørnedalen is also quite far from the city, but both are close to the nature area in the North of the Island.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The pricing was okay, a little expencive if you end up in a place where you share kitchen and bathroom.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found it okay to know what to send in, and was slightly confused about if I had been accepted or not. It took very long to get a response back (end may) but they were nice to communicate with (especially Musta).

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Send in 5 documents: passport, some sort of language assessment, learning agreement, transcript of records and something else. And then wait 2 months. 
The forhåndsgodkendelse needs to be done before sending the application so you have to apply for this as soon as possible.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email answers from the university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was accepted into all.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do everything as early as possible so that you can get help if anything does not work. And it makes sence to choose your courses as early as possible.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had two courses with only a little obligatory things to do, which made it possible to dedicate all the needed time for the third (this was lucky as you could not see what the course load is before you start).

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were good, but introductory so not very deep into the subject.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot of people choose to read things on their own instead of coming to the lectures, which is the opposite than at home. Also there was no way to organize the courses with each other as some things and lectures simply overlap, and they do not care.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Bio-2005 - Biologiske ressurser i nord
 Bio-2506 - Introduction to fish biology
 Bio-2508 - Aquaculture I

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Biologiske ressurser i nord – really cool course, with a lot of excurtions, (this course is in norwegeian) but I would highly recommend it. We did cool things like fishing in Alta and cutting up a reindeer. 
Introduction to fish biology – this course was good, I learned a lot, but the course load was massive, handing in more than 100 pages during the semester. 
Aquaculture I – this course was quite beginner, and would have been better in person (than online) – half of the executions were cancelled.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I was surprised at how many nice outdoor things I ended up buying and how easy it is to plan expensive trips to different places in Norway.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
(I did not take out a special insurance, this cost is my insurance from home)

The food was quite expensive, but that was expected, it is definitely possible to spend less money than this. Beer and alcohol was very expensive though, recommend bringing a bottle from home to get you started. 
-	 The phone bills in Norway were really expensive so I ended up just keeping my danish phone number, this worked well, (and was possible with Call Me)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not use these very much as there are so many things to do, but was satisfied with what I did try.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
TSI is a big sports organisation with many undergroups, like swimming, skiing, climbing, sailing, hiking….
There is also the big Kraft training center on campus that is very nice. 
Socially speaking there were several clubs at school like knitting and walking that we were invited to weekly in an email form the school. 
Also the ESN groups planed a lot of good events for meeting others in the beginning.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All the ESN events, and definitely to use Turbo to borrow ski, bikes and tents and camping gear.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: In town the polar museum and the aquarium. For trips Ersfordsboten, Lyngen alps, sommarøya, senya are all places reachable by public transport, and are good for small camping trips. Otherwise a longer trip to Lofoten or Finland. (go whale watching)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It very much like home

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to all the social events in the beginning of the year

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really, the biggest challenge is the language barrier with some of the other international students.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I very much liked the respect and use of nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1.Get out there and make some good friends, also important to make good friends that live close. 
2.Take the time to enjoy the weather and nature
3.You do not need to pack a lot of summer clothes, autumn and winter comes quickly.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont worry just enjoy

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: meeting people from different placing and getting to know their culture, and making friends for life, in a beautiful place.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Trying to balance studying and exploring
2. Finding the right people to be friends with (as it can sometimes be hard to cross the language barrier. 
3. It got to cold to go camping way before I was ready to stop exploring.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
